title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Implementing the Judicial Responsibility System and Improving the Trial Supervision and Management Mechanism (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Implementing the Judicial Accountability System and Improving the Trial Supervision and Management Mechanism (Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2017] No. 11

To fully implement the reform of the judicial accountability system, properly handle the relationship between full delegation of power and effective supervision, standardize the trial supervision and management duties of presidents and division heads of people's courts, and effectively address issues such as unwillingness to delegate power, reluctance to supervise, and inability to manage properly, the following opinions are put forward regarding the improvement of the trial supervision and management mechanism of people's courts, in accordance with the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on Improving the Judicial Accountability System of People's Courts and other relevant regulations:

1. After the completion of the reform of the post-based judge system, people's courts at all levels must strictly implement the reform requirements of the judicial accountability system, ensuring that "those who adjudicate cases are responsible for the adjudications." Except for cases discussed and decided by the judicial committee, presidents and division heads shall no longer review and approve the written judgments of cases in which they did not directly participate in the trial, nor shall they approve cases in a disguised manner through oral instructions, observing collegial panel deliberations, or sending written judgments for review.

2. People's courts at all levels shall gradually improve the list of powers of presidents and division heads for trial supervision and management. The duties of presidents and division heads for trial supervision and management are mainly reflected in the review and approval of procedural matters, comprehensive guidance of trial work, supervision of the unification of adjudication standards, full-process supervision of trial quality and efficiency, and exclusion of extraneous factors interfering with trial activities.

Presidents and division heads may, within their scope of duties and authority, view, operate, and monitor the operation of trial processes, analyze the trial operation situation, prompt corrections of improper conduct, supervise the progress of case trials, and coordinate arrangements for rectification measures. The timing, content, nodes, and outcomes of the exercise of trial supervision and management duties by presidents and division heads shall be fully recorded and permanently preserved on the office and case-handling platform.

3. People's courts at all levels shall establish a case assignment mechanism based primarily on random case assignment and supplemented by designated case assignment. According to the categories of trial fields and arrangements for streamlining simplicity and complexity, the judge responsible for hearing a case shall be randomly determined. Where specialized collegial panels or professional trial teams have been established, cases shall be randomly assigned within the collegial panel or trial team. Once a judge responsible for a case is determined, he or she shall not be changed without authorization. Where a change of the judge responsible for a case is truly necessary due to grounds such as withdrawal, job transfer, health conditions, or integrity risks, the change shall be approved by the president or division head within his or her authority, and the reasons and results of the change shall be promptly notified to the parties and publicized on the office and case-handling platform.

Cases may be assigned by designation under any of the following circumstances: (1) major, difficult, complex, or new types of cases that are necessary for the president or division head to undertake; (2) batch cases or related cases where the plaintiffs or defendants are the same, the causes of action are the same, and two or more cases are accepted in the same batch; (3) cases retried by the court; (4) cases where the president or division head proposes a designation for case assignment based on the need for individual case supervision; (5) other cases unsuitable for random case assignment. The circumstances of designated case assignment shall be fully recorded on the office and case-handling platform.

4. For cases that are legally to be tried by a collegial panel, the collegial panel shall in principle be formed randomly. For relatively fixed trial teams and collegial panels formed due to the need for specialized adjudication, personnel shall be regularly rotated and adjusted, generally for a period not exceeding two years.

People's courts at all levels may, based on the number of post-based judges and cases, have the president or division head designate a judge with seniority and strong trial-presiding ability within the collegial panel to serve as the presiding judge, or may explore having the judge responsible for the case serve as the presiding judge. When a president or division head participates in the trial of a case as a member of the collegial panel, he or she shall serve as the presiding judge.

5. For cases that meet any of the circumstances set forth in Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on Improving the Judicial Accountability System of People's Courts, the president or division head has the right to require the sole judge or collegial panel to report on the progress and the results of the deliberation. If the president or division head disagrees with the trial process or the results of the deliberation of the relevant case, he or she shall not directly change the opinion of the collegial panel but may decide to submit the case to a professional judges' meeting or the judicial committee for discussion.

Where, during the trial of a case, the sole judge or collegial panel discovers that the case falls under the above circumstances for individual case supervision, it shall proactively report to the president or division head in accordance with procedures and fully record it on the office and case-handling platform. For cases that fall under specific types of individual case supervision circumstances, the ordinary procedure shall in principle apply.

6. People's courts at all levels shall fully leverage the role of professional judges' meetings and judicial committees in summarizing trial experience and unifying adjudication standards. On the basis of improving working mechanisms such as reference to similar cases and adjudication guidelines, a mandatory retrieval mechanism for similar cases and related cases shall be established to ensure the unification of adjudication standards and the unity of legal application for similar cases.

Presidents and division heads shall promptly identify and address issues of inconsistency in adjudication standards and legal application through means such as individual case supervision of specific types, participation in professional judges' meetings or judicial committees, reviewing case evaluation results, analyzing cases reversed or remanded, hearing opinions from courts within the jurisdiction, and handling various types of petitions and complaints.

7. People's courts at all levels shall strengthen the application of information platforms, effectively promote the simultaneous entry, generation, and archiving of electronic case files, and deeply integrate them with office and case-handling platforms, so as to realize automated supervision functions such as recording and tracking of completed matters, prompting and urging of matters to be completed, timed warnings for matters approaching deadlines, and timely freezing of prohibited operations.

8. People's courts at all levels shall conscientiously implement the main responsibility and supervisory responsibility of the Party for improving Party conduct and ensuring integrity, and shall consciously accept legal supervision from the authorities, democratic supervision from the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, procuratorial supervision, public opinion supervision, and social supervision, so as to continuously improve the level of fair adjudication. Organizational and personnel departments, disciplinary inspection and supervision departments, trial management departments, and trial business departments shall strengthen coordination and cooperation, form a synergy of internal supervision, and insist on holding accountable for dereliction of duty and strict accountability.

9. Upon receiving complaints, reports, or reflections involving trial personnel, presidents and division heads shall investigate and verify in accordance with regulations. Untrue reports shall be promptly closed and clarified, and those who fail to truthfully explain the situation or whose reports are verified shall be dealt with in accordance with discipline and law. If the cases involved have not yet been concluded or enforced, presidents and division heads may supervise the handling according to law and, in accordance with procedural regulations, adjust the judge responsible for the case, members of the collegial panel, or trial support personnel; if the cases have been concluded, they shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of the procedural laws.

10. These Opinions shall be implemented on a trial basis as of May 1, 2017.

April 12, 2017
